newsitem.title: YEMEN: First foreign observers arrive for Yemen poll.
newsitem.headline: First foreign observers arrive for Yemen poll.

text.p: Four election observers from Britain have arrived in Yemen, the first group of monitors to arrive ahead of the Arab country's April 27 parliamentary poll, the British Embassy in Sanaa said on Thursday.

"They will be working in Yemen for one month, observing the state of preparations up to now, the campaign stage, polling day itself, the counting of votes and the immediate aftermath of the elections," the embassy said in a statement.
The mission is funded by the British government.
The four observers -- two men and two women -- are the first of some 280 foreign observers expected to monitor the elections.
Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh last month invited international observers to Yemen to ensure a fair ballot.
Election officials expect about 5,000 candidates to seek votes for 301 parliamentary seats under the banners of 12 parties or as independents.

Four opposition groups, including the country's main opposition Yemen Socialist Party (YSP), have said they would boycott the elections, the first since a 1994 civil war nearly tore apart Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest countries.
Yemeni opposition groups have objected to alleged irregularities in the voter registration.

International observers monitored the last poll in 1993 when 22 parties vied for 301 seats in parliament. Saleh's General People's Congress won a majority, followed by the Islamist Islah Party and the YSP.
